title: The Big Bang of 1687
notes: p1.1 and p1.2 run in reverse order (conclusion before set-up). Narration on p1.1 opens on Glauka and the Ottoman guards; p1.2 then carries 'two thousand years'.
p1.2: the church and mosque insets are drawn as separate domed buildings; really the Parthenon itself was converted. Narration says the same building changed.

p3.4: the caption 'Remember: an explosion, not time.' breaks the voice bible ('never says Remember:'). It is lettered; narration paraphrases without it. Patch to 'An explosion, not time.' if regenerating.
p2.1: a field cannon is drawn rather than a mortar. Minor.

panels.visual: The Parthenon as a mosque with a minaret, Ottoman guards on the Acropolis walls, calm blue sky, Glauka on a column
panels.caption: It was a temple, then a church, then a mosque.
panels.narr: Hoo. I've sat on these columns a very long time. In my day this was a temple. Later it was a church, then a mosque, with a minaret on the side.

panels.visual: The building complete under its roof across the centuries, three small inset pictures: a temple with a golden statue, a church with a cross, a mosque with a crescent
panels.caption: For two thousand years the Parthenon kept its roof.
panels.narr: Gods changed. Prayers changed. The building didn't. For two thousand years the Parthenon stood almost whole, roof and all.

panels.visual: Venetian ships and an army camp under General Morosini at the foot of the Acropolis, cannons smoking, banners with winged lions
panels.caption: In 1687 a Venetian army under Morosini besieged the Acropolis.
panels.narr: Then, in 1687, a Venetian army under General Morosini besieged the Acropolis: they surrounded it and attacked. Ottoman Turks held the top. The Venetians wanted it.

panels.visual: Inside the Parthenon, Ottoman soldiers stacking barrels of gunpowder under the old roof, a sweat drop
panels.caption: The Ottomans stored gunpowder inside the Parthenon.
panels.narr: Ottoman soldiers needed a strong place for their gunpowder, so they stored it inside the Parthenon, barrel after barrel. One spark was all it would take.

panels.visual: A big mortar firing from a hill, a flaming shell in the air over Athens, long curved speed lines
panels.caption: Morosini's guns fired on the Acropolis.
panels.narr: Morosini's guns fired on the Acropolis. Shell after shell went up, and came down on rock and wall. Then one came down somewhere else.

panels.visual: Close-up of a mortar shell dropping through a hole in the roof of the Parthenon, the barrels of gunpowder below, tiny white dots of fear
panels.caption: A mortar shell came through the roof.
panels.narr: A mortar shell came through the roof. Straight down, into the room full of barrels.

panels.visual: Black silhouette of the Parthenon with the middle blowing apart in white-hot light, columns flying, smoke; shown wide and vivid
panels.caption: 26 September 1687.
panels.direction: Say the date, then silence for the DOOOM.

panels.visual: Smoke clearing over the half-ruined Parthenon: broken columns in rubble, a tiny Glauka looking down
panels.caption: About three hundred people died.
panels.narr: (pause) When the smoke cleared, the middle of the Parthenon was gone. About three hundred people died.

panels.visual: The ruined Parthenon at dawn, with empty spaces where the middle was, Glauka perched on a broken column
panels.caption: It is a ruin because of an explosion, not old age.
panels.narr: In the morning I came back to my column. Two thousand years of standing, undone by one shell. It is a ruin because of an explosion, not old age.

panels.visual: A big close-up of the broken column drums scattered, hand-drawn arrows showing the missing middle
panels.caption: The middle of the building blew apart.
panels.narr: Look where the arrows point. The middle of the building blew apart, and columns from both long sides came down in pieces.

panels.visual: Modern tourists with cameras climbing the Acropolis steps with a tiny girl-and-owl pointing up
panels.caption: Today we visit what is left.
panels.narr: Today we visit what is left. Crowds climb these steps every day to see a building that was blown up, not worn down.

panels.visual: Glauka the owl flying right at us with a cute stern face, caption box beside her
panels.caption: Remember: an explosion, not time.

speech.speaker: Glauka
speech.text: Gunpowder stored in a temple, always a bad idea.

panels.narr: That's history: it happened, and the proof is the gap in the middle of each long side. An explosion, not time. Go and find it.
